prompt:
A black-and-white CHILDREN'S COLORING BOOK page, square 1:1, 1080x1080. Composition must be SQUARE, never wide or landscape.

CRITICAL — READ FIRST: (a) the drawing must BLEED OFF ALL FOUR EDGES with NO frame, NO border line, NO box and NO white margin band; (b) there must be NO starburst, no radiating burst, no sparkle rays and no sunbeam rays anywhere in the picture; (c) use a ZOOMED-IN composition where the main character runs past every edge of the square, so nothing floats in empty white space.

SCENE: We are looking INSIDE one giant friendly ANIMAL CELL, drawn so big that its soft wobbly membrane edge sweeps diagonally across the top-left corner and every other part of the cell runs off the bottom, left and right edges of the picture — like peeking through a window into a cosy round one-room home.
- The cell's OUTER EDGE is one thick, gently bumpy, wavy line (its soft skin — no bricks, no wall), cutting across the upper-left corner and running off both edges there. Outside that line, in the corner, just a few plain drifting bubbles.
- In the middle sits the NUCLEUS, the biggest character: a big round boss with a wide happy face (two big round eyes with pupils, cheerful eyebrows, a big open smile), wearing a simple round librarian's reading glasses pushed up on its forehead, its round body edged with a tidy row of small porthole circles.
- Around the nucleus, its little organelle friends, all with simple happy faces, all LARGE and CHUNKY and partly CUT OFF by the picture edges:
- Two BEAN-shaped mitochondria buddies at the bottom, each with three or four big wavy ribbon stripes inside, one flexing its stubby arms like a proud little power-lifter, half cut off by the bottom edge.
- A GOLGI pancake-stack friend on the right: four flat pancakes piled up with a happy face on the top pancake, sliding little round parcels off its edge, half cut off by the right edge.
- A long wavy RIBBON-SLIDE (the endoplasmic reticulum) curving from the nucleus toward the lower left and off the left edge, dotted along its back with a row of small round dot friends riding it like a slide.
- One round LYSOSOME bubble friend with big cheeks happily munching a cookie-crumb, tucked near the bottom right, cut off by the edge.
- Two small barrel friends (the centrioles) stacked in a T shape like little drums, near the nucleus.
- A loose scatter of tiny plain dots (ribosomes) and two or three long soft curvy threads (the cytoskeleton) weaving between the friends and running off the edges.
- Everything is drawn LARGE, SIMPLE and CHUNKY, with generous open white areas inside every shape so a child can colour them in.

STYLE — coloring book line art:
- BOLD, THICK, EVEN BLACK OUTLINES on pure WHITE. Every shape fully closed.
- ABSOLUTELY NO shading, NO grey tones, NO hatching, NO stippling, NO cross-hatching, NO gradients, NO colour fill, NO solid black areas anywhere (eyes may have a small solid pupil only).
- Simple, cheerful, chunky cartoon shapes with plenty of white space.

STRICTLY FORBIDDEN — the page is rejected if any of these appear:
- ANY decorative STARBURST, comic-style radiating burst, "pow"/impact star, sparkle burst, twinkle burst, sunbeam rays, radiating speed lines, motion rays or halo of rays behind, around or under any character. NO radiating lines of any kind anywhere.
- ANY rectangle, rounded rectangle, square box outline, picture frame, panel edge, comic panel, border line, outer margin line, ground-line box, shelf, table, counter or vignette. The drawing must NOT sit inside a box of any kind. Do NOT draw a thin black line anywhere near the edge of the image. There must be NO white margin between the artwork and the image edge.
- The artwork must BLEED OFF ALL FOUR EDGES of the square — the membrane line runs off the top-left corner and the organelle friends are CUT OFF by the bottom, left and right edges.
- NO text, letters, numbers, words, captions, labels or watermarks anywhere.
- NO speech bubble, thought bubble or balloon of any kind (one is added separately afterwards).
- NO human figures, no real flames, no arrows.
